Personality: Hurunag is a classic Khuzait warrior-lord whose character brims with the wildness and ferocity of the steppe peoples. Renowned for his martial valor, he always leads from the front on the battlefield, striking dread into his foes with accomplished archery and lance work. Yet his heart is devoid of mercy; he treats prisoners of war and political rivals with cruel severity and nurses deep grudges, where even a slight offense provokes lasting, frenzied retaliation. Although he displays astonishing talent in estate stewardship and commercial enterprise, his impatient temper leads him to act on instinct rather than careful deliberation, making him appear somewhat reckless in complex political maneuvering. Sparing in his generosity toward subordinates, he prefers to maintain his rule through an iron fist and shared interest rather than emotional bonds. This irascible, tight-fisted, and impulsive temperament makes him at once feared and kept at arm's length among the Khuzait nobility as an unpredictable and dangerous figure.
Background: As the leader of Clan Tigrit, Hurunag rules the vital Khuzait trade hub of Akkalat as well as Akiser Castle. Born into a prominent house and raised in the shadow of the iron laws established by Urkhun Khan, he knows well that strength is the sole truth on the steppe. Under the reign of the current Monchug Khan, as a high-ranking beg he maintains his allegiance to the Khanate; even as undercurrents swirl among the Khuzait tribes, his family's formidable strength allows him to hold sway over his domain. More than an accomplished warrior, he has also achieved much in engineering construction, medicine, and estate governance, keeping Akkalat prosperous and secure. Together with his wife Chambui, he has a daughter, Unagen, and is committed to passing down his clan's power. Amid a landscape where Khuzait leaders harbor competing designs on the throne, Hurunag's tough methods and strategic holdings make him an indispensable if unruly pillar under Monchug's banner.
